html:
The Amazonian Kichwa are Quechua speaking peoples of the rainforest of eastern Ecuador, in the provinces of Napo, Pastaza, Sucumbíos and Orellana, with kin in northern Peru. They call themselves Runa, "people".

Their ancestors were forest peoples who took up a form of Quechua, probably as a trade and mission language, during the colonial era. Groups include the Napo Kichwa and the Canelos Kichwa of the Pastaza. They live by farming manioc, hunting and fishing, and are known for their painted pottery.

In 2012 the Inter-American Court of Human Rights ruled that Ecuador had violated the rights of the Kichwa community of Sarayaku by letting an oil company onto its land without consent. Their neighbours include the Waorani, the Sápara and the Andean Kichwa.
